chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from al-Husayn ibn Hammad, from Isḥaq, from 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever enters Mecca with an 'Umrah and stays until the hilal (crescent) of Dhu al-Hijjah, then it is not permissible for him to leave until he performs Hajj with the people.

key_terms.هِلَالِ: Hilal (crescent moon, marking the start of a month)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who performs 'Umrah and stays in Mecca until the crescent of Dhu al-Hijjah appears?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing the principle of 'Umrah al-Mubtala' (Umrah performed during Hajj months) where staying until the 1st of Dhu al-Hijjah obligates the pilgrim to perform Hajj in that same year. This highlights the Shia juristic view that the intention and duration of stay transform the ritual status, ensuring the pilgrim fulfills the primary pillar of Hajj after completing the minor pilgrimage. The ruling underscores the interconnectedness of the two pilgrimages in the sacred months, preventing the separation of Umrah and Hajj when the pilgrim remains in the holy city through the critical transition period.
